description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral lung opacities and mediastinal shift.
description.detailed_description: This is an anteroposterior chest radiograph showing bilateral lung fields. There is significant opacification of the right hemithorax, with a mediastinal shift towards the left, suggesting volume loss or mass effect on the right side. The left lung appears hyperinflated, likely compensatory. The diaphragm on the right side is elevated. No visible air-fluid levels or clear pleural effusion are noted.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing right upper lobe consolidation.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph showing increased opacification in the right upper lobe, consistent with consolidation. The heart and mediastinal contours appear normal. The left lung field is clear. No obvious pleural effusion or pneumothorax is visible. The bony structures, including the ribs and clavicles, appear intact.
visible_findings: no visible pleural effusion or pneumothorax

description.short_caption: Chest CT showing a large cavitary lesion in the right lung.
description.detailed_description: This axial chest CT image reveals a large cavitary lesion in the right lung with thickened walls and internal air-filled spaces. The left lung appears relatively normal in this slice. The mediastinum is midline, and no significant pleural effusion is visible. The findings are suggestive of a necrotizing process, such as an abscess or cavitary infection.
visible_findings: large cavitary lesion in the right lung
normal-appearing left lung in this slice

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph at six-month follow-up showing residual abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph showing both lung fields, the heart, and the mediastinum. There is evidence of residual abnormalities in the right upper lung field, including increased opacity suggestive of scarring or fibrosis. The left lung appears relatively clear. The mediastinum is midline, and no significant pleural effusion or pneumothorax is visible. The bony structures, including ribs and clavicles, appear intact.
visible_findings: increased opacity in the right upper lung field

description.short_caption: Lateral chest radiograph showing abnormal lung findings.
description.detailed_description: This is a lateral chest radiograph showing the thoracic cavity. There is evidence of abnormal opacification in the right lung field, with possible consolidation or mass effect. The lung markings appear distorted, and there may be volume loss or pleural thickening. The heart and diaphragm are partially visible, with no clear abnormalities in these structures. The image is of diagnostic quality and demonstrates findings suggestive of a pulmonary pathology.
visible_findings: abnormal opacification in the right lung field
possible volume loss or pleural thickening
